subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Expected Utility: The Old Model
description: A micro-lesson that makes Expected Utility: The Old Model usable.

hook.text: For 300 years, economists assumed people weigh costs and benefits like calculators. They don't.

buildup.text: Expected utility theory says a rational person always picks the option with the highest expected value.

discovery.text: Bernoulli proposed this in 1738. It works on paper. But people routinely violate it in experiments.

twist.text: Allais showed people prefer a sure $1 million over a gamble worth more in expected value. We're not calculators.

climax.text: Expected utility describes how people should decide. Prospect theory describes how they actually do.

punchline.text: Rationality is a theory. Behavior is the data.

quiz.question: What did Allais's paradox reveal?
options: People prefer sure gains over higher-value gambles
Expected utility theory was never useful
